title: Degreewise bijectivity of the coproduct Cech restriction map
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], I a finite set, U_i and V objects of X_et, f_i:U_i→X and f_V:V→X their maps to the identity object, and c_i:U_i→V satisfy c_i f_V=f_i. Suppose the underlying scheme cocone (V,c_i) is a coproduct [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Let S_1 and S_2 be chosen Cech products [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] for U_i and the singleton V respectively, and F an abelian etale sheaf [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Fix p≥0 and maps g_t:S_1.W(p,t)→S_2.W(p,0) whose k-th projection is S_1.pr(p,t,k) followed by c_(t(k)). Then s↦(t↦F(g_t)(s(0))) is a bijection from S_2.cochains(F,p) to S_1.cochains(F,p). Here 0 denotes the unique tuple with values in Fin 1.

source.place: Tag 03OZ, lemma-cech-complex, equation-sheaf-coprod and the following product decomposition

proof.text: By the colimit universal property, identify the underlying scheme of V with the coproduct of U_i, with c_i the coprojections [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Since c_i f_V=f_i, its induced map to X is the coproduct of the U_i structure maps. Apply [lem-sc-etale-fibre-product-coproduct] in degree p to obtain the decomposition of its (p+1)-fold fibre product into the tuple-indexed fibre products of the U_i.

Compare these Over X products with the chosen products S_1.W(p,t) and S_2.W(p,0) using their universal properties [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]. A compatible family of projections in X.Etale has a unique map into the chosen object; conversely the underlying scheme fibre product has a unique map with those projections and the resulting map to X is etale. These two maps are inverse by projection uniqueness and lift to X.Etale. The component equation of the decomposition shows that its t-th inclusion is g_t, since g_t has exactly those projections. Thus g_t are disjoint open immersions covering S_2.W(p,0), by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family].

The inclusions form a covering in the small etale site because they are jointly surjective and open immersions are etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Apply the proved upstream Scheme.Etale.isIso_piLift_of_disjoint [lem-weil-pbc-disjoint-etale-sections-product] to these monic disjoint covering inclusions. Its sheaf equalizer argument [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] is as follows. On diagonal overlaps the two projections agree, since the inclusions are monomorphisms. On off-diagonal overlaps the scheme is empty, and the empty covering forces its section group to be zero. Therefore every tuple of sections is compatible and has a unique amalgamation. Restriction from F(S_2.W(p,0)) to the tuple of F(S_1.W(p,t)) is bijective. Since every map Fin(p+1) to Fin 1 is the constant zero map, evaluation at that map identifies S_2.cochains with F(S_2.W(p,0)); its inverse is the constant tuple. This proves the displayed bijectivity, including empty I.

lean.statement:
theorem etale_coproduct_cech_restriction_bijective
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (I : Type u) [Finite I]
    (U : I → X.Etale) (f : ∀ i, U i ⟶ Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X))
    (V : X.Etale) (fV : V ⟶ Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X))
    (c : ∀ i, U i ⟶ V)
    (hc : IsColimit (Cofan.mk V.left (fun i => (c i).left)))
    (hw : ∀ i, c i ≫ fV = f i)
    (S₁ : SiteCechComplex U f)
    (S₂ : SiteCechComplex (fun _ : Fin 1 => V) (fun _ => fV))
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (p : ℕ)
    (g : ∀ t : Fin (p + 1) → I, S₁.W p t ⟶ S₂.W p (fun _ => 0))
    (hg : ∀ t k, g t ≫ S₂.pr p (fun _ => 0) k = S₁.pr p t k ≫ c (t k)) :
    Function.Bijective (fun s : S₂.cochains F.obj p =>
      (fun t => F.obj.map (g t).op (s (fun _ => 0)) : S₁.cochains F.obj p))
